local TRANSFORM_SECONDS = 0.8  -- companion <-> weapon
local HUB_SECONDS = 0.6        -- every change passes through the branch
local GROW_SECONDS = 1.6       -- branch -> companion (first growth)

local SHAPES = { -- branch silhouettes: segment count, curve, cluster placement
	Spear  = { Segments = 5, Curve = 0.02, ClusterAt = "Tip",   Scale = 1.15 },
	Katana = { Segments = 5, Curve = 0.22, ClusterAt = "Curve", Scale = 1.00 },
	Scythe = { Segments = 6, Curve = 0.55, ClusterAt = "Arc",   Scale = 1.25 },
	Hammer = { Segments = 3, Curve = 0.05, ClusterAt = "End",   Scale = 0.90 },
}

local state = {} -- [UserId] = { Model, Form, Bond, BondT, Root }

local function part(parent, size, cf, color, material, name)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Size = size; p.CFrame = cf; p.Color = color
	p.Material = material or Enum.Material.Wood
	p.Anchored = true; p.CanCollide = false; p.Name = name or "Part"
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

local function blossom(parent, cf, s)
	-- one pink quartz blossom: five petals around a bright heart
	for i = 1, 5 do
		local a = (i / 5) * math.pi * 2
		part(parent, Vector3.new(0.22, 0.22, 0.22) * s,
			cf * CFrame.new(math.cos(a) * 0.22 * s, math.sin(a) * 0.22 * s, 0),
			QUARTZ, Enum.Material.Glass, "Petal")
	end
	local heart = part(parent, Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2) * s, cf, QUARTZ_LIGHT, Enum.Material.Neon, "Heart")
	local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
	light.Color = QUARTZ; light.Range = 4; light.Brightness = 0.6
	light.Parent = heart
	return heart
end

local function buildBranch(player, typeName)
	local shape = SHAPES[typeName]; if not shape then return nil end
	local model = Instance.new("Model"); model.Name = "BranchDaemon"
	local base = CFrame.new()
	local pos = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0); local ang = 0
	for i = 1, shape.Segments do
		ang += shape.Curve
		local seg = part(model, Vector3.new(1.1, 0.28, 0.28) * shape.Scale,
			base * CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, ang), WOOD, Enum.Material.Wood, "Limb")
		if i == 1 then model.PrimaryPart = seg end
		pos += Vector3.new(math.cos(ang) * 1.0 * shape.Scale, math.sin(ang) * 1.0 * shape.Scale, 0)
		blossom(model, base * CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, ang), 0.8)
	end
	blossom(model, base * CFrame.new(pos), 1.5) -- the crown cluster: the future quartz heart of the weapon
	model.Parent = workspace
	return model
end

local function buildCompanion(player, species)
	-- Stylized server builds in the part grammar of Chapter 34;
	-- the Studio display models carry the full sculpted detail.
	local model = Instance.new("Model"); model.Name = species .. "Companion"
	local body = part(model, Vector3.new(1.2, 1.6, 0.7), CFrame.new(0, 1.4, 0), WOOD, Enum.Material.Wood, "Body")
	model.PrimaryPart = body
	part(model, Vector3.new(0.8, 0.8, 0.8), CFrame.new(0, 2.7, 0), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Head")
	if species == "Fox" then
		part(model, Vector3.new(0.3, 0.9, 0.3), CFrame.new(-0.25, 3.3, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, 0.2), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Ear")
		part(model, Vector3.new(0.3, 0.9, 0.3), CFrame.new(0.25, 3.3, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, -0.2), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Ear")
		local tail = part(model, Vector3.new(0.7, 1.8, 0.7), CFrame.new(0, 1.6, 0.9) * CFrame.Angles(0.7, 0, 0), QUARTZ, Enum.Material.Glass, "BlossomTail")
		blossom(model, tail.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 1, 0), 1.3)
	elseif species == "Serpent" then
		for i = 1, 4 do
			part(model, Vector3.new(0.8, 0.5, 0.8), CFrame.new(0, 0.4, i * 0.7) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, i * 0.15), WOOD, Enum.Material.Wood, "Coil")
		end
		part(model, Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), CFrame.new(0, 2.6, 0.4), QUARTZ, Enum.Material.Glass, "ScaleCrest")
	elseif species == "BearCub" then
		part(model, Vector3.new(1.5, 1.2, 1.0), CFrame.new(0, 1.1, 0), WOOD, Enum.Material.Wood, "CubBody")
		for _, x in ipairs({ -0.6, 0.6 }) do
			local paw = part(model, Vector3.new(0.5, 0.4, 0.6), CFrame.new(x, 0.25, -0.5), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Paw")
			part(model, Vector3.new(0.4, 0.2, 0.3), paw.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, -0.1, -0.3), QUARTZ, Enum.Material.Neon, "QuartzClaws")
		end
	elseif species == "Sprite" then
		part(model, Vector3.new(0.3, 1.1, 0.3), CFrame.new(-0.3, 0.5, 0), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Leg")
		part(model, Vector3.new(0.3, 1.1, 0.3), CFrame.new(0.3, 0.5, 0), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood, "Leg")
		blossom(model, CFrame.new(0, 3.35, 0), 1.2) -- the blossom crown
	end
	blossom(model, CFrame.new(0, 2.05, -0.4), 1.0) -- the heart blossom, shared by every species
	model.Parent = workspace
	return model
end

local function setForm(player, form)
	local st = state[player.UserId]; if not st then return end
	st.Form = form
	player:SetAttribute("BranchState", form)
	if st.Model then st.Model:Destroy(); st.Model = nil end
	local typeName = player:GetAttribute("WeaponType")
	if form == "Branch" and typeName then
		st.Model = buildBranch(player, typeName)
	elseif form == "Companion" then
		st.Model = buildCompanion(player, player:GetAttribute("CompanionSpecies") or "Sprite")
	end
end

function _G.JadeBranchOnChoice(player, typeName)
	if TWIN_BLOOM_USER_ID ~= 0 and player.UserId == TWIN_BLOOM_USER_ID then return end
	state[player.UserId] = state[player.UserId] or { Form = "None", Bond = 0 }
	setForm(player, "Branch")
	task.delay(GROW_SECONDS, function()
		if state[player.UserId] and state[player.UserId].Form == "Branch" then
			setForm(player, "Companion") -- the Answer: it looks at its keeper first (follow code turns it so)
		end
	end)
end

function _G.JadeBranchOnHit(player)
	local st = state[player.UserId]; if not st then return end
	local now = os.clock()
	local b = st.Bond or 0
	if st.BondT then b = math.max(0, b - (now - st.BondT) * 6) end
	st.Bond = math.min(100, b + 8); st.BondT = now
	player:SetAttribute("BranchBond", math.floor(st.Bond))
end

local function watchCharacter(player, char)
	local function onTool(tool)
		if not tool:IsA("Tool") then return end
		local st = state[player.UserId]; if not st or st.Form == "Weapon" then return end
		player:SetAttribute("BranchState", "Transforming")
		task.delay(TRANSFORM_SECONDS, function()
			if state[player.UserId] then setForm(player, "Weapon") end
		end)
		tool.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent)
			if parent == nil and state[player.UserId] then
				setForm(player, "Branch") -- through the hub, always
				task.delay(HUB_SECONDS, function()
					if state[player.UserId] and state[player.UserId].Form == "Branch" then
						setForm(player, "Companion")
					end
				end)
			end
		end)
	end
	char.ChildAdded:Connect(onTool)
	for _, c in ipairs(char:GetChildren()) do onTool(c) end
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char) watchCharacter(player, char) end)
	if player.Character then watchCharacter(player, player.Character) end
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	local st = state[player.UserId]
	if st and st.Model then st.Model:Destroy() end
	state[player.UserId] = nil
end)

-- Follow: branch and companion hold station at the keeper's left,
-- bobbing gently; the companion turns to face the keeper's facing
-- (the Answer, every frame, not just on arrival).
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(t)
	local now = os.clock()
	for userId, st in pairs(state) do
		local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(userId)
		local char = player and player.Character
		local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if root and st.Model and st.Model.PrimaryPart then
			local bob = math.sin(now * 1.6 + userId % 7) * 0.18
			local target = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(-3.2, st.Form == "Branch" and 1.2 or 0, 1.2)
			if st.Form == "Companion" then
				target = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(-3.2, -2.6, 1.2) -- feet near the keeper's ground line
			end
			local cur = st.Model.PrimaryPart.CFrame
			st.Model:SetPrimaryPartCFrame(cur:Lerp(target + Vector3.new(0, bob + 2.6, 0), 0.12))
		end
		if st.BondT and now - st.BondT > 0.25 then -- decay the visible bond
			st.Bond = math.max(0, (st.Bond or 0) - 6 * (now - st.BondT)); st.BondT = now
			local p = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(userId)
			if p then p:SetAttribute("BranchBond", math.floor(st.Bond)) end
		end
	end
end)

-- Jade Spirit | 47_Wings.server.lua
-- Location: ServerScriptService > insert Script, rename it Wings
-- What it does: THE FOUR WINGS (Chapter 36). Wings -- not outfits --
-- are this game's primary visual customization. Four types, all
-- pink and brown, each paired with a flight style:
--
--   Feathered  pink feathers, brown tips. THE STARTER WINGS:
--              granted with flight itself (Susanoo Stage 3 --
--              15,000 Lifetime + 100 Essence, Scripts 35/39).
--   Crystal    brown wooden frame, pink quartz membranes.
--              Unlock: reach the Crystal Deep (10,000 Lifetime,
--              Script 19) and craft at the Workbench for Blooms.
--   Butterfly  pink-and-brown patterned. Unlock: free 100 Thorn
--              Husks (Script 4's count) -- the garden's gratitude.
--   Dragon     brown scales, pink membranes. Unlock: hold the
--              Tree through 10 Hollow assaults (Script 31) -- the
--              endgame wings. (A wing TYPE any keeper can earn;
--              Oakley's Gold Dragon is a Daemon, not a wing, and
--              is untouched by this Script.)
--
-- * FLIGHT ITSELF NEVER CHANGES: Script 39 owns flight -- Stage 3,
--   stamina 100 draining 26/s, the stage speed table. Wing types
--   tune FEEL inside those caps (the style table below: climb,
--   glide, turn multipliers, each between 0.9 and 1.1, published
--   in Chapter 36). Top speed and stamina are identical for every
--   wing. Style is the ladder; power is not for sale or unlock.
-- * Selection is by NAME from this whitelist, validated here;
--   ownership is re-checked on every select and on every join.
--   Unlocks persist in DataStore "JadeWings_v1" (a set of type
--   names) and are published as attributes: WingType (worn now)
--   and four OwnsWing<Type> booleans Script 48 renders.
-- * Flight-style application: this Script publishes WingClimb,
--   WingGlide, WingTurn attributes from the style table; Script 39
--   may read them as multipliers inside its own caps (documented
--   hook -- if it does not, the wings are purely visual and every
--   number in Chapter 36 still holds).

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local WING_TYPES = {
	Feathered = { Climb = 1.0, Glide = 1.1, Turn = 1.0 },
	Crystal   = { Climb = 1.1, Glide = 0.9, Turn = 1.0 },
	Butterfly = { Climb = 0.9, Glide = 1.1, Turn = 1.1 },
	Dragon    = { Climb = 1.1, Glide = 1.0, Turn = 0.9 },
}
local CRAFT_BLOOMS = 25 -- Crystal wings, paid in Crystal Blooms at the Workbench

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("JadeWings_v1")
local owned = {} -- [UserId] = { [typeName] = true }

local selectEvent = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
selectEvent.Name = "JadeWingSelect"
selectEvent.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local function publish(player)
	local set = owned[player.UserId] or {}
	for name in pairs(WING_TYPES) do
		player:SetAttribute("OwnsWing" .. name, set[name] == true)
	end
	local worn = player:GetAttribute("WingType")
	if worn and WING_TYPES[worn] then
		local s = WING_TYPES[worn]
		player:SetAttribute("WingClimb", s.Climb)
		player:SetAttribute("WingGlide", s.Glide)
		player:SetAttribute("WingTurn", s.Turn)
	end
end

local function grant(player, name, save)
	owned[player.UserId] = owned[player.UserId] or {}
	owned[player.UserId][name] = true
	if save then
		local list = {}
		for k in pairs(owned[player.UserId]) do table.insert(list, k) end
		pcall(function() store:SetAsync(tostring(player.UserId), list) end)
	end
	publish(player)
end

-- Called by the systems that EARN wings (documented hooks; each
-- caller is itself server-side and already counts the deed).
function _G.JadeGrantWing(player, name)
	if WING_TYPES[name] then grant(player, name, true) end
end

-- Flight unlock (Stage 3) grants the starter wings: Script 35/39
-- may call this at the Stage-3 transition; the attribute watch
-- below also catches it, so the grant cannot be missed.
local function watchStage(player)
	local function check()
		if (player:GetAttribute("SusanooStage") or 0) >= 3 then
			if not (owned[player.UserId] and owned[player.UserId].Feathered) then
				grant(player, "Feathered", true)
				if not player:GetAttribute("WingType") then
					player:SetAttribute("WingType", "Feathered"); publish(player)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("SusanooStage"):Connect(check)
	check()
end

local function onJoin(player)
	owned[player.UserId] = {}
	local saved
	pcall(function() saved = store:GetAsync(tostring(player.UserId)) end)
	if type(saved) == "table" then
		for _, name in ipairs(saved) do
			if WING_TYPES[name] then owned[player.UserId][name] = true end
		end
	end
	publish(player)
	watchStage(player)
end

selectEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, name)
	if type(name) ~= "string" or not WING_TYPES[name] then return end
	if not (owned[player.UserId] and owned[player.UserId][name]) then return end
	player:SetAttribute("WingType", name)
	publish(player)
end)

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onJoin)
for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do task.spawn(onJoin, p) end
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player) owned[player.UserId] = nil end)

Your character stands IN the light while you choose — visible to other players as a keeper in the gate, petals drifting up around them. There is no loading screen and no fade
3 · Choose (in the UI) | Pick a world card and confirm Travel — or step backward out of the sheet / press the close control, and the UI dissolves, the ripple settles, and nothing has happened: browsing the gate costs nothing and commits to nothing
4 · Travel (on confirm) | The swirl closes over your character in a spiral of petals — pink for a homebound or low-danger world, pink darkening toward grey-green as the destination's danger rises — a one-second white-pink bloom of light, and you arrive at that world's spawn, facing its gate, which is already swirling: the way back is in your first eyeline, always. Your companion/Daemon arrives beside you in the same bloom
5 · Return (any gate, any world) | Every world contains at least one return gate of the same design. Walking through it opens the same UI with HOME — the Floating Island Hometown — pinned first and always available at 0. Returning asks nothing, at any health, mid-horde (Chapter 3): the gate is the one promise the apocalypse cannot break
The transition never lies about danger:  The petal spiral's color at Beat 4 is the destination's danger made visible before arrival — full pink for the safe and gentle worlds, grey-green creeping in for the Deep Ruins and beyond. A young keeper who picks a hard world sees the grey come into the light while there is still a full second to remember the choice. The gate warns with its beauty, not with a pop-up.
Element | Design
Panel | A centered panel, about 80% of screen width on phone, dark wood frame with a pink crystal blossom in its top corners — the gate's plaque, become a screen. Title: CHOOSE YOUR WORLD. Beneath it, one line that never moves: YOUR SWING COUNT — [Lifetime thrusts], in the count's own gold. Every lock on this screen is measured against that number, and the player can see it while they browse
World cards | One card per world, in ladder order, scrollable. Each card carries: the world's name; a small painted thumbnail (the Chapter 3 concept art, cropped); its GATE — 'Open' in jade, or 'Needs 25,000 lifetime thrusts' in grey; a DANGER row of 0–5 thorn marks; a REWARDS line naming its best reason to go; and, for locked worlds, a progress bar (your count / required) and the exact shortfall — '690 to go'. No card hides its number
States | OPEN: full color, blossom corner lit, Travel button live. LOCKED: the card desaturated to grey-green — the apocalypse palette doing UI work — with the requirement and progress bar in place of the Travel button; tapping it shows one kind line: what the world holds and the count that opens it (the same honesty as Script 20's refusal card). CURRENT: the world you are standing in is marked YOU ARE HERE and its Travel button is disabled
Confirm | Travel requires a deliberate second tap: tap a card to select it (it lifts, its thumbnail brightens, its danger and rewards lines expand), then tap TRAVEL THROUGH THE GATE. One tap never moves a player. Close / step back cancels at any point before the second tap
Party | If you are in a party, the panel's foot shows your party's faces; TRAVEL offers 'Take my party' when every member meets the gate — and names, by name, any member who does not yet, with their shortfall. A party is never split silently and never held back without the reason on screen
Home pinned | HOME — the Floating Island Hometown — is always the first card, always Open, from every gate in every world. Safety is one decision away at all times; the ladder only ever gates going OUT and DOWN, never coming home
Input | Touch: tap card, tap Travel. Controller: left stick moves card focus, A selects, A again on Travel confirms, B closes. Keyboard: arrow keys + Enter, Esc closes. The UI is a ScreenGui in StarterGui named GateGui (build steps below) and works identically on Xbox, because travel itself is server-driven

The sky is part of the arena:  From anywhere in the apocalypse valley, looking up past the fog, you can see HOME: the floating island in the sky above — its waterfalls falling toward the clouds, the hometown's lanterns, and the Giant Pink Crystal Cherry Blossom Tree's crown in pink light. It never moves and it is never hidden for long: the fog parts, the storm breaks, and there it is. Every keeper on the hill is literally fighting under their own home. Build the sightline first (Step 2 below) and protect it in every later placement: no ruin, dead tree, or arena wall may permanently block the hilltop's view of the island.
Element | Design
The valley bowl | One enclosed valley, about 900 × 900 studs, ringed by broken cliffs and dead slopes that close the world without invisible walls where a wall would do. The HILL stands at its exact center (next section). Four approach roads run from the valley's edge gates and spawn pockets to the hill — north road (the Gate Road), east road (the Village Road), south road (the Shrine Road), west road (the Bamboo Road) — each a distinct fight with a distinct landmark (below)
Ruined Japanese buildings | The valley was a town like the hometown, and it shows the same architecture RUINED: about 60 ruined buildings — wooden houses with collapsed tiled roofs, a fallen five-story pagoda leaning at 15 degrees with two floors pancaked (a climbable landmark and sniper perch), a market row of shattered stalls, a bathhouse with a cracked, fog-filled tub hall. Build ONE house in four ruin states (intact-frame, roof-fallen, burned-out, rubble) and instance the set; interiors stay enterable — ruins are cover, loot rooms, and ambush rooms, never facades
Broken torii | Torii in every state of loss along the roads: one snapped at a pillar, one toppled face-down across the north road (crawl-under cover), one lintel-less pair of pillars marking the old shrine, and at each safe pocket a small INTACT torii whose pink crystal still glows — the visual grammar of Chapter 40, reused: crystal lit = safety, crystal dark = the Sleep
Dead cherry trees | About 45 dead sakura: grey-brown twisted trunks, bare branches clawing, no blossom — EXCEPT the hilltop's own dead tree (below) and a rule that sells the whole world: when a wave is fully freed, the nearest dead tree to the hill blooms pink for one minute, then fades. Hope, on a timer, visible from the whole valley. One blossom tree stands at each safe pocket, kept alive by its shrine — the pockets' beacons in the fog
Green fog zones | The Sleep made visible: GREEN FOG banks (Part-based fog volumes in the low ground between the rings, plus Lighting fog tinted to match at distance) that pool in the Deep Ruins hollows and drift slowly along the roads. Fog zones hide zombie spawns (the horde shambles OUT of fog, Chapter 3), muffle sound, and cut view distance to about 40 studs inside. Standing in green fog is a choice with a price: salvage nodes cluster in it. Fog is never on the hilltop — the hill is the one clear-sighted place, which is why everyone wants it
Ground & palette | Cracked grey earth, ash drifts, dead grass, toppled lanterns (dark), split stone paths, dim cracked crystal outcrops whose light is GREEN-grey, not pink. The palette law (Chapter 3) inverts completely: the only warm pink in the whole world is the island in the sky, the safe pockets' crystal, gate light, the keepers themselves — and the hill's crystal (next section), when it is held
Feature | Design
Form | A single broad hill at the valley's center: about 180 studs across at the base, rising about 35 studs in three terraced rings to a flat circular summit about 60 studs across. Terraces are the fight's geography: the summit is the point; Terrace 2 (the mid ring, about 110 across) is the close fight; Terrace 1 (the base ring) is where waves first meet defenders. Four ramps — one per road — climb the terraces at the cardinal points; between ramps, the slopes are steep, rubble-choked scramble (climbable at half speed): the hill can be rushed from any side, but only the ramps allow speed, Daemon mounts, and retreat
The summit | A ruined shrine plaza: cracked stone circle 60 across, a broken ring of standing stones, four toppled lanterns — and at its exact center, THE HILL CRYSTAL: a single pink crystal shard, 8 studs tall, grown from a dead cherry tree's split trunk — the HILL TREE, a dead sakura whose branches hold the crystal like a cupped hand. The crystal is the point's face: dark and grey-green when the hill is unheld, kindling pink as keepers hold it, full pink bloom-light when the hill is WON for the round (below). Every player in the valley can read the game's state off that crystal's color at a glance
Sightlines | From the summit: all four roads end-to-end, every ring, the safe pockets' torii glow, and — up — the floating island. From the roads: the summit crystal visible at every bend. Oakley's overwatch (Chapter 36) owns two built perches: the fallen pagoda (east, off the hill) and the summit's own broken standing-stone ring, sized for one ghillie keeper and her rifle's lanes down all four ramps
Why one hill | King of the Hill concentrates the whole server's fight into one shared story: everyone sees the same crystal, defends the same ramps, hears the same wave horns. A sprawling world would scatter twelve players across a map built for a hundred; one valley and one hill keep every session full, legible, and finishable — a round is a complete story (next sections) in the game's 20–30 minute session (Chapter 2)
Ring | Where | What lives and happens there
The Apron | The hill's base ring and the first 50 studs of each road | Wave staging and the breath before contact: sleeping husks, the first salvage, fallen parties regrouping. Zombies enter here from the roads in ones and twos between waves — pressure, never a flood
The Ruins | The ruined town ring, 50–250 studs from the hill's base | The mid fight: zombie wanderers and packs among the ruined houses, resource nodes in the fog hollows, the fallen pagoda and market row. Parties dart out here between waves to salvage — and get caught here when the next wave horn sounds
The Deep Ruins | 250+ studs out, the valley's edge hollows and cliff bases | The spawn wilderness: green fog at its thickest, the wave muster grounds (below), the densest salvage and the Crystal Deep-style caves at the south cliff. Nobody holds ground here; even Oakley's lanes end in fog. Waves are BORN here and walk the roads to the hill
The Outer Shrines | Four raid shrines, one on each road at the Ruins / Deep Ruins boundary | The defense game's outer line (Script 31): a wave that breaks a shrine's meter walks that road unopposed to the hill. Holding shrines thins the hill fight; losing one never ends the round — it makes the hill harder, which the crystal's color announces to everyone
Thing | Place | Design
The Fallen Pagoda | East Ruins, off the Village Road | The leaning five-story pagoda: climbable interior ramps, the valley's best overwatch perch, one boss arena (below) in its shadow court
The Drowned Bathhouse | South Ruins | Fog-interior salvage vault: the thickest indoor fog, the richest single node cluster, zombie sleepers in the tubs — enter quiet, leave fast
The Toppled Torii | North road, Apron edge | The face-down torii across the road: crawl-under cover on the main wave road, the north chokepoint every defense plan starts with
Safe pockets (4) | At each road's Outer Shrine, and one at the valley spawn gate | A 20-stud circle around a small intact torii with LIT pink crystal: inside it, zombies will not enter (the light curtain law, Chapter 3, at pocket scale), health and Daemon sync restore, and the return gate stands here. Pockets are recovery, not camping: a pocket's crystal dims while its shrine's meter (Script 31) is broken, and waves walk PAST a dim pocket to the hill — shelter is earned by the shrine line, never free forever
Boss arenas (3) | The Pagoda Court (east), the Shrine of the First Road (north summit approach), the Drowned Court (south) | Walled courts that seal (thorn gates rise) when a boss wakes (Chapter 40's boss list, staged here): the court is the fight — cover rings, one crystal lamp, no fog. A boss freed unseals its court and blooms its nearest dead tree for a full round
Resource nodes | Fog hollows, ruins interiors, cave mouths | Salvage nodes (dead-crystal clusters, fallen lantern oil, shrine offerings): gathered between waves, worth Spend-side salvage and Atelier materials, respawning on the wave clock so the economy of a round is: hold the hill, dart for nodes, be back before the horn. Nodes never spawn on the summit — the hill pays in control, not loot (scoring, below)
Mechanic | Rule
The control zone | The summit circle, 60 studs across, marked by the standing-stone ring and a ground ring that lights when occupied. Control is measured INSIDE this circle only — Terrace 2 is the fight, the summit is the score
Accruing control | While at least one keeper stands in the circle AND no zombie stands in it, the hill accrues CONTROL TIME for the party/server at 1 second per second, shown on the crystal and the HUD as the round's Hill Time. A zombie inside the circle CONTESTS it: accrual pauses (it never reverses) until the circle is cleared. Keepers do not fight each other for it — this is a co-op hill: every keeper's time adds to the same shared Hill Time, because the enemy is the Sleep, not each other (no PvP, Chapter 3, holds even here)
The crystal reads the game | Hill Crystal states, visible valley-wide: DARK (no keeper has held this round / hill lost), KINDLING (accruing — pink light rising with unbroken hold time), BLOOM (a hold milestone reached — full pink light, a petal burst over the summit, the nearest dead trees bloom). The crystal is the scoreboard the world itself displays
Hold milestones | Unbroken holds of 60 / 180 / 300 seconds are HOLD EVENTS: each fires a valley-wide chime, a salvage rain at the summit's edge (never inside the circle), and a wave delay — the Sleep recoils. Milestones are the round's chapters: a party's story is told in how many it reached
Losing the hill | If every keeper leaves or falls and a zombie stands in the circle for 10 unbroken seconds, the hill is LOST for that wave: the crystal goes dark, accrued Hill Time is KEPT (banked, next section and Chapter 42), and the next wave comes harder. The hill can always be retaken — King of the Hill here has no elimination, only the endless return of the fight, which Chapter 42 makes the mode's whole law
Daemon & Susanoo on the hill | Daemons count as presence for holding ONLY while ridden or in Beast state inside the circle beside their keeper — a parked Daemon holds nothing. Susanoo manifestations overhang the circle legitimately at Stage 4+: their shield gifts (Chapter 30) apply on the summit exactly as anywhere, corruption targets only
Score line | How it accrues | Where it lives
Hill Time | Shared server total of control seconds (above); the round's headline number | The crystal, the HUD, and the round summary (Chapter 42)
Frees | Every zombie and husk freed, by keeper — personal and party totals | Personal lines feed titles and the Legends Gallery round board at the island's Hero's Plaza
Survival Time | From a keeper's first step through the gate to their fall (Chapter 42) | The survival leaderboard — the mode's permanent record
Swing count | Every connecting swing, exactly as Chapter 4 counts it — the hill changes nothing about the count, and the count is banked even in death (Chapter 42) | Lifetime + Spend Balance, Script 13
-- Jade Spirit | 29_HollowGrove.server.lua
-- Location: ServerScriptService > insert Script, rename it HollowGrove
-- What it does: the Hollow Grove (Chapter 25) -- a corrupted island
-- where Thorn Skeletons rise in waves and experienced Keepers farm
-- them. Unlock: 25,000 lifetime thrusts, through Script 19's gate.
-- Skeletons that escape the Hollow are also the corruption that
-- assaults the Great Blossom Tree itself (Script 13 runs those
-- events); this zone is where the corruption lives.
--
-- RISK AND REWARD, IN THE OPEN:
-- * A skeleton laid to rest pays its killer BONUS thrusts (Balance only) --
--   the fastest balance faucet in the game, priced in Chapter 25.
--   It pays the killer named by Script 2's creator tag, once, from
--   this Script. Kills never touch Lifetime: the thrusts that landed
--   were already counted when they connected. Farming here fills a
--   wallet; it cannot forge a history.
-- * Skeletons HURT: their strike is real damage, waves scale, and a
--   fall restarts your wave progress in spirit if not in code --
--   you respawn at the lobby and run back in while the wave you
--   left keeps coming. High risk, high reward, no death tax:
--   nothing is taken from a player who falls. Ever.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local ZONE_CENTER = workspace:WaitForChild("ZoneCenter_HollowGrove", 15)
local ZONE_RADIUS = 130
local TEMPLATE_NAME = "ThornSkeletonTemplate"
local INTERMISSION = 15
local MAX_ALIVE = 24

local wave = 0
local alive = {} -- [model] = { Humanoid, Root, LastBite }
local waveActive = false
local zoneOccupied = false

local function inZone(root)
	if not ZONE_CENTER or not root then return false end
	return (root.Position - ZONE_CENTER.Position).Magnitude <= ZONE_RADIUS
end

local function playersInZone()
	local list = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		local root = p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if root and inZone(root) then table.insert(list, p) end
	end
	return list
end

local function killReward(waveNumber)
	return 6 + waveNumber -- bonus thrusts to the killer
end

local function isBossWave(n)
	return n % 5 == 0
end

local function spawnSkeleton(waveNumber, boss)
	local template = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(TEMPLATE_NAME)
	if not template then
		warn("[Jade Spirit] ThornSkeletonTemplate missing in ServerStorage (Chapter 25, build steps).")
		return nil
	end
	local skel = template:Clone()
	skel.Name = "HollowSkeleton"
	local humanoid = skel:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local root = skel:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not humanoid or not root then skel:Destroy() return nil end
	local hp = (boss and 400 or 50) + 25 * (waveNumber - 1) * (boss and 2 or 1)
	humanoid.MaxHealth = hp
	humanoid.Health = hp
	humanoid.WalkSpeed = boss and 11 or 9 + math.min(5, waveNumber * 0.3)
	humanoid:SetAttribute("IsThornHusk", true) -- Script 2 can hit it
	humanoid:SetAttribute("IsHollowSkeleton", true)
	if boss then skel:ScaleTo(1.6) end
	local angle = math.random() * math.pi * 2
	local dist = math.random(30, 70)
	skel.Parent = workspace
	skel:MoveTo(ZONE_CENTER.Position + Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * dist, 3, math.sin(angle) * dist))
	alive[skel] = { Humanoid = humanoid, Root = root, LastBite = 0, Boss = boss }
	humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
		local entry = alive[skel]
		alive[skel] = nil
		-- Pay the killer Script 2's tag names, re-validated.
		local tag = humanoid:FindFirstChild("creator")
		local killer = tag and tag.Value
		if killer and killer:IsA("Player") and killer.Parent then
			_G.JadeGrantBonus(killer, killReward(wave), "SkeletonKill")
			if _G.JadeGrantSusanooEssence then
				_G.JadeGrantSusanooEssence(killer, entry and entry.Boss and 15 or 2, "SkeletonKill")
			end
			-- Exclusive drops (Chapter 25): the Hollow provides.
			local roll = math.random()
			if entry and entry.Boss then
				_G.JadeGrantItem(killer, "HollowSeed", 1)
				if roll < 0.12 and _G.JadeGrantSusanooEssence then
					_G.JadeGrantSusanooEssence(killer, 25, "BossDrop")
				elseif roll < 0.37 then
					_G.JadeGrantItem(killer, "BoneBow", 1)
				end
			else
				if roll < 0.04 then
					_G.JadeGrantItem(killer, "HollowSeed", 1)
				elseif roll < 0.05 then
					_G.JadeGrantItem(killer, "HollowCharm", 1)
				end
			end
		end
		-- Burst of dark petals: corruption coming apart.
		for _ = 1, 10 do
			local petal = Instance.new("Part")
			petal.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
			petal.Size = Vector3.new(0.5, 0.14, 0.5)
			petal.Color = Color3.fromRGB(90, 60, 110)
			petal.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
			petal.CanCollide = false
			petal.CanTouch = false
			petal.CanQuery = false
			petal.CFrame = root.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0)
			petal.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(math.random(-6, 6), math.random(5, 11), math.random(-6, 6))
			petal.Parent = workspace
			Debris:AddItem(petal, 1.2)
		end
		task.delay(0.3, function() skel:Destroy() end)
	end)
	return skel
end

-- ---------- wave director ---------------------------------------------
local function aliveCount()
	local n = 0
	for _ in pairs(alive) do n += 1 end
	return n
end

local function startWave()
	wave += 1
	waveActive = true
	local count = math.min(4 + wave * 2, MAX_ALIVE)
	for i = 1, count do
		task.delay(i * 0.7, function()
			if zoneOccupied then spawnSkeleton(wave, false) end
		end)
	end
	if isBossWave(wave) then
		task.delay(3, function()
			if zoneOccupied then spawnSkeleton(wave, true) end
		end)
	end
end

local function waveClearedBonus()
	-- Everyone standing in the Hollow when a wave falls shares its
	-- bonus: the farm rewards the group that held the ground.
	if wave % 5 == 0 then
		for _, p in ipairs(playersInZone()) do
			_G.JadeGrantBonus(p, 100, "WaveCleared")
		end
	end
end

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(1)
		local occupants = playersInZone()
		zoneOccupied = #occupants > 0
		if not zoneOccupied then
			if waveActive or aliveCount() > 0 then
				for skel in pairs(alive) do skel:Destroy() end
				alive = {}
				wave = 0
				waveActive = false
			end
			continue
		end
		if not waveActive then
			task.wait(INTERMISSION)
			if #playersInZone() > 0 then startWave() end
		elseif aliveCount() == 0 then
			waveClearedBonus()
			waveActive = false
			task.wait(INTERMISSION)
			if #playersInZone() > 0 then startWave() end
		end
		-- Skeleton behaviour: shamble at the nearest Keeper; bite on
		-- contact with a per-skel cooldown. All server-run.
		local now = os.clock()
		for skel, entry in pairs(alive) do
			local humanoid, root = entry.Humanoid, entry.Root
			if humanoid.Health > 0 then
				local best, bestDist, bestRoot = nil, math.huge, nil
				for _, p in ipairs(occupants) do
					local pRoot = p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
					local pHum = p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
					if pRoot and pHum and pHum.Health > 0 then
						local d = (pRoot.Position - root.Position).Magnitude
						if d < bestDist then best, bestDist, bestRoot = pHum, d, pRoot end
					end
				end
				if bestRoot then
					humanoid:MoveTo(bestRoot.Position)
					if bestDist <= 4 and now - entry.LastBite >= 1 then
						entry.LastBite = now
						best:TakeDamage(entry.Boss and 14 or 8)
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end)

local statue = workspace:WaitForChild("GuardianStatue", 15)

local PLAQUE_TEXT = "THE GUARDIAN WHO WOULD NOT FALL\n"
	.. "When the Hollow came for the Tree, the first Guardian\n"
	.. "gave her name, her crown, and her head — and kept her post.\n"
	.. "Her bow still watches the Grove. Her spear still thrusts\n"
	.. "in every Keeper's hands. Protect the Tree, and she is never gone."

if statue then
	local plaque = statue:FindFirstChild("StatuePlaque")
	if plaque then
		local gui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
		gui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
		gui.Parent = plaque
		local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		label.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(38, 32, 30)
		label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(240, 225, 200)
		label.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
		label.TextScaled = true
		label.Text = PLAQUE_TEXT
		label.Parent = gui
	end

	-- The crystal flame above the empty neck: jade and steady while
	-- the Statue stands, guttering when its integrity falls (Script
	-- 31 publishes the meter), gone only while it is Fallen.
	local flame = statue:FindFirstChild("StatueFlame")
	if flame and flame:IsA("BasePart") then
		local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
		light.Color = Color3.fromRGB(140, 255, 200)

-- Jade Spirit | 31_DefenseSystem.server.lua
-- Location: ServerScriptService > insert Script, rename it DefenseSystem
-- What it does: THE DEFENSE OF THE THREE (Chapter 26). The village,
-- the Great Blossom Tree, and the Guardian Statue share one fate and
-- one system: three global meters -- Village, Tree, Statue -- kept
-- in a DataStore, published as workspace attributes, drained by
-- corruption assaults, healed by Keepers' thrusts, and defended
-- together. Every other system reads the attributes; only this
-- Script moves the meters.
--
-- THE GUARDIAN WALKS AMONG THEM: while the exclusive owner's
-- account is in the server (the SAME UserId pasted in Script 8 --
-- paste it below too), defenses are stronger in three concrete,
-- code-visible ways: assault drains run at 60% speed, assault
-- skeletons spawn with 80% health, and the lowest meter quietly
-- regenerates. This is the lore made mechanical. It changes no
-- damage number any player deals, sells nothing, and cannot be
-- transferred: her presence is the buff, and presence cannot be
-- botted by anyone who is not her.
--
-- Kid-safe stakes: a meter at zero is FALLEN, never destroyed. The
-- village closes its shops and hides, the Tree withers to Critical,
-- the Statue's flame goes out -- and all three heal back over time
-- and with thrusts. Nothing the corruption does is permanent.
-- Permanence is the players' side of the story.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local EXCLUSIVE_USER_ID = 0 -- << REPLACE with the same UserId as Script 8

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("JadeDefense_v1")
local METER_MAX = 1000
local SAVE_SECONDS = 30
local ASSAULT_INTERVAL = 1200 -- 20 minutes between assaults
local ASSAULT_LENGTH = 240

local METERS = { "Village", "Tree", "Statue" }
local health = { Village = METER_MAX, Tree = METER_MAX, Statue = METER_MAX }
local loaded = false

local defenseEvent = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("JadeDefenseEvent")
if not defenseEvent then
	defenseEvent = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	defenseEvent.Name = "JadeDefenseEvent"
	defenseEvent.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end

local function guardianPresent()
	if EXCLUSIVE_USER_ID == 0 then return false end
	return Players:GetPlayerByUserId(EXCLUSIVE_USER_ID) ~= nil
end

local function publish()
	for _, m in ipairs(METERS) do
		workspace:SetAttribute(m .. "Health", math.floor(health[m]))
		workspace:SetAttribute(m .. "Fallen", health[m] <= 0)
	end
	workspace:SetAttribute("GuardianPresent", guardianPresent())
	workspace:SetAttribute("ThreatLevel", workspace:GetAttribute("ThreatLevel") or 0)
end

-- Loading: retried, fail-quiet. A failed load starts the meters full
-- for the session and disables saving (Script 1's doctrine: a bad
-- read must never become a bad write over the world's real state).
for _ = 1, 3 do
	local ok, data = pcall(function()
		return store:GetAsync("meters_v1")
	end)
	if ok then
		loaded = true
		if type(data) == "table" then
			for _, m in ipairs(METERS) do
				health[m] = math.clamp(tonumber(data[m]) or METER_MAX, 0, METER_MAX)
			end
		end
		break
	end
	task.wait(1)
end

local function saveMeters()
	if not loaded then return end
	pcall(function()
		store:SetAsync("meters_v1", health)
	end)
end

function _G.JadeHealMeter(meter, amount)
	if not health[meter] then return end
	amount = math.clamp(tonumber(amount) or 0, 0, 50)
	health[meter] = math.clamp(health[meter] + amount, 0, METER_MAX)
	publish()
end

function _G.JadeDamageMeter(meter, amount)
	if not health[meter] then return end
	amount = math.clamp(tonumber(amount) or 0, 0, 50)
	health[meter] = math.clamp(health[meter] - amount, 0, METER_MAX)
	publish()
end

function _G.JadeGetMeter(meter)
	return health[meter] or 0
end

local NPC_LINES = {
	Calm = { "The Tree is safe. We thrust on.", "Lovely blossoms today.", "Mind the petals, Keeper." },
	Alarmed = { "Did you hear that? Bones...", "Stay near the gates!", "The corruption is close." },
	Shelter = { "Inside! Inside!", "Guard the door, Keepers!", "The Guardian will come..." },
}

local function setThreat(level)
	workspace:SetAttribute("ThreatLevel", level)
	for _, npc in ipairs(npcs) do

-- ---------- assaults -----------------------------------------------------
local TARGETS = {
	Village = { Anchor = "VillageHeart", Drain = 3, ZoneRadius = 90, Display = "the Village" },
	Tree = { Anchor = "TreeHitbox", Parent = "GreatBlossomTree", Drain = 4, ZoneRadius = 60, Display = "the Great Blossom Tree" },
	Statue = { Anchor = "StatueBase", Drain = 3, ZoneRadius = 60, Display = "the Guardian Statue" },
}
local assaultIndex = 0
local assaultActive = false

local function anchorFor(targetKey)
	local spec = TARGETS[targetKey]
	if spec.Parent then
		local parent = workspace:FindFirstChild(spec.Parent)
		return parent and parent:FindFirstChild(spec.Anchor)
	end
	return workspace:FindFirstChild(spec.Anchor)
end

local function spawnAssaultSkeleton(anchor, guardian)
	local template = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("ThornSkeletonTemplate")
	if not template then return nil end
	local skel = template:Clone()
	skel.Name = "AssaultSkeleton"
	local humanoid = skel:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local root = skel:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not humanoid or not root then skel:Destroy() return nil end
	local hp = guardian and 60 or 75
	humanoid.MaxHealth = hp
	humanoid.Health = hp
	humanoid.WalkSpeed = 10
	humanoid:SetAttribute("IsThornHusk", true)
	humanoid:SetAttribute("IsAssaultSkeleton", true)
	local angle = math.random() * math.pi * 2
	skel.Parent = workspace
	skel:MoveTo(anchor.Position + Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * 55, 3, math.sin(angle) * 55))
	return { Model = skel, Humanoid = humanoid, Root = root }
end

local function runAssault(targetKey)
	if assaultActive then return end
	local spec = TARGETS[targetKey]
	local anchor = anchorFor(targetKey)
	if not anchor then return end
	assaultActive = true
	local guardian = guardianPresent()
	local startHealth = health[targetKey]
	setThreat(2)
	defenseEvent:FireAllClients("AssaultStarted", spec.Display, guardian)

	local skels = {}
	local toSpawn = 8
	local spawned = 0
	local deadline = os.clock() + ASSAULT_LENGTH
	while os.clock() < deadline do
		task.wait(1)
		-- trickle spawns to the cap
		local aliveNow = 0
		for _, z in ipairs(skels) do
			if z.Humanoid.Health > 0 then aliveNow += 1 end
		end
		if spawned < toSpawn and aliveNow < 6 then
			local z = spawnAssaultSkeleton(anchor, guardian)
			if z then table.insert(skels, z) spawned += 1 end
		end
		-- skels march on the target and chew it
		local draining = 0
		for _, z in ipairs(skels) do
			if z.Humanoid.Health > 0 then
				local d = (z.Root.Position - anchor.Position).Magnitude
				if d > 9 then
					z.Humanoid:MoveTo(anchor.Position)
				else
					draining += 1
				end
			end
		end
		if draining > 0 then
			local rate = spec.Drain * math.min(draining, 5) * (guardian and 0.6 or 1)
			_G.JadeDamageMeter(targetKey, rate) -- per second tick
		end
		local allDead = spawned >= toSpawn
		for _, z in ipairs(skels) do
			if z.Humanoid.Health > 0 then allDead = false break end
		end
		if allDead then break end
		if health[targetKey] <= 0 then break end
	end

	-- survivors crumble; the event is judged by what it cost
	for _, z in ipairs(skels) do
		if z.Humanoid.Health > 0 then z.Model:Destroy() end
	end
	local lost = startHealth - health[targetKey]
	local repelled = lost < 400 and health[targetKey] > 0
	defenseEvent:FireAllClients(repelled and "AssaultRepelled" or "AssaultWithered", spec.Display, guardian)
	if repelled then
		for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
			_G.JadeGrantBonus(p, 75, "Defense")
			local root = p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
			if root and (root.Position - anchor.Position).Magnitude <= spec.ZoneRadius + 40 then
				_G.JadeGrantBonus(p, 75, "DefenseAtPost") -- 150 total at post
			end
		end
	end
	setThreat(0)
	assaultActive = false
end

task.spawn(function()
	publish()
	setThreat(0)
	while true do
		task.wait(ASSAULT_INTERVAL)
		if #Players:GetPlayers() > 0 then
			assaultIndex = (assaultIndex % #METERS) + 1
			runAssault(METERS[assaultIndex])
		end
	end
end)

-- Passive recovery + the Guardian's quiet watch.
task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(10)
		for _, m in ipairs(METERS) do
			if health[m] > 0 and health[m] < METER_MAX and not assaultActive then
				health[m] = math.min(METER_MAX, health[m] + 2) -- slow bloom-back
			elseif health[m] <= 0 then
				health[m] = math.min(METER_MAX, health[m] + 1) -- even fallen things return
			end
		end
		if guardianPresent() and not assaultActive then
			local lowest = METERS[1]
			for _, m in ipairs(METERS) do
				if health[m] < health[lowest] then lowest = m end
			end
			health[lowest] = math.min(METER_MAX, health[lowest] + 5)
		end
		publish()
	end
end)

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(SAVE_SECONDS)
		saveMeters()
	end
end)
game:BindToClose(saveMeters)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(publish)
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function()
	task.delay(2, publish)
end)
publish()

Element | Design
Where it lives | The gate flow (Chapter 40): after a player selects an apocalypse world on the world-selection panel and before Travel confirms, the panel's card expands into the DIFFICULTY SELECTOR for that run. Solo players pick for themselves; a party's gate panel shows one selector, set by the party leader, with every member's panel mirroring the choice — a round has ONE difficulty, shared by everyone in it, and the panel says so
The five choices | Five cards in a row (stacked on phone): EASY / NORMAL / HARD / NIGHTMARE / ETERNAL. Each card carries, in this order: the swings-per-zombie number in the largest type on the card ('3 SWINGS PER ZOMBIE'); the zombie's ward (health) in damage points; what that means per zombie in counted swings earned; the reward multipliers (below); and a danger line in plain words ('For a first run.' / 'The horde will stand in front of you a long time.')
Your power, shown honestly | Because swing power grows on the account (Chapter 43), each card ALSO shows the swings-per-zombie at YOUR current power: 'At your swing power (40): 2 swings.' The selector never promises a number your own growth has already changed — the table below is the reference at starting power, and the card computes your real one live
Lock-in | Difficulty locks at Travel and cannot change mid-round — no dropping to Easy when the wave turns, no raising to Nightmare to farm a beaten wave. Leaving through a gate ends your run at that difficulty; the next run picks fresh. The locked difficulty rides the HUD all round beside the wave number, and the round summary (below) is stamped with it
Default & first run | NORMAL is preselected, and a first-time crosser's panel carries one extra line: 'Most keepers start on Normal. Easy is a warm-up, not a failure.' Difficulty is a dial the player owns — the game never auto-raises it, never shames a lower pick, and never gates a world behind a difficulty: worlds gate on Lifetime count (Chapter 40), difficulty is chosen INSIDE them
Difficulty | Swings per zombie (at reference power 25) | Zombie ward (damage) | Counted swings earned per zombie | Hill-score multiplier | Salvage & shard multiplier | Who it is for
Easy | 1 | 25 | 1 | ×1 | ×1 | First runs, young keepers, learning a new world — the horde falls as fast as you can swing, and so does its pressure
Normal | 3 | 75 | 3 | ×1.5 | ×1.25 | The designed round: a zombie holds your attention through a full Bloom Chain, and a wave is a real fight
Hard | 5 | 125 | 5 | ×2 | ×1.5 | Parties who hold milestones on Normal and want the hill to push back — five swings is a long time at a chokepoint
Nightmare | 10 | 250 | 10 | ×3 | ×2 | Full parties and Oakley's overwatch lanes: every zombie is a commitment, every free is an event — and every zombie pays ten swings into everyone's gates, tiers, and pet levels
Eternal | 20 | 500 | 20 | ×5 | ×3 | The legend difficulty: a single zombie outlasts a combo, a chain, and a Daemon transformation. Chosen rarely, remembered always; its rounds are short and its counts are enormous
Why the multipliers are not on the count:  The swing count itself is NEVER multiplied — a swing is a swing is a swing, on every difficulty, because the count is the game's one honest number (Chapters 4 and 38): it gates worlds, tiers, and pet levels, and a multiplied count would let difficulty choice counterfeit the record those gates read. Difficulty's generosity flows where generosity is safe: hill score and salvage — the round's glory and the round's loot — multiply freely (above), while progression grows the natural way, by the extra swings the harder zombie honestly demanded. Nightmare's ten-swing zombie is not a ×10 button; it is ten real swings, stood for and landed.
Wave band | Zombies per wave | Alive at once (cap) | Zombie speed | Zombie strength | Notes
Wave 1 | 6 | 6 | 8 studs/s (a shamble) | Contact bump only; ward = difficulty ward | A teaching wave: one road only (north), the crystal kindles for the first time
Waves 2–3 | 10 / 14 | 10 | 8.5 / 9 | Same ward; bump-back grows slightly | Second road opens at Wave 2; Outer Shrine pressure begins at Wave 3
Waves 4–6 | 18 / 22 / 26 | 16 | 9.5 → 10.5 | Ward +10% per wave from Wave 4 (rounded to whole swings at reference power where possible) | Fog musters thicken; first boss wakes at Wave 5 (Pagoda Court or Shrine Court by round seed)
Waves 7–9 | 30 / 34 / 38 | 22 | 11 → 12 | Ward +10% per wave; every third zombie is an armored Hollow (double ward) | All four roads active; shrine meters under real pressure; hold milestones get scarce
Waves 10–12 | 42 / 46 / 50 | 28 | 12.5 → 13.5 | Ward growth continues; armored share rises to one in two | Boss at Wave 10; the lull between waves shrinks from 75 s toward 45 s
Wave 13 onward | 50 + 4 per wave, uncapped | 32 (the engine's honest ceiling — pressure beyond this comes from speed and ward, never from invisible extras) | 14, then +0.5 every 3 waves, capped at 16 (player walk speed — beyond this they cannot be outrun at all, and the design does not pretend otherwise) | Ward +10% per wave, uncapped; armored share to two in three | THE OVERWHELM BAND: the curve is no longer tuned to be beaten. From here, the round is a countdown the party can read — hold time is heroism, and the fall (below) is the designed ending, arriving on schedule
Beat | What happens
1 · The overwhelm (the moment itself) | When a keeper's guard finally breaks under the horde, time eases for one second around them (a local slow, cosmetic only): the nearest zombies stop at arm's length instead of piling on — the Sleep is patient, and the image is a keeper ringed, not mauled. Their weapon's light gutters like a candle
2 · The standing sleep | Thorns of soft grey-green light rise around the keeper and hold them upright, asleep standing — the exact visual language of the Thorn Husks, because that is the fiction: a keeper who falls does not die, they JOIN the sleep they were fighting, and everyone watching understands the whole game in one picture. Their companion/Daemon curls around their feet and sleeps with them — together in the fall, as in everything (Chapter 34)
3 · The banking (the rewarding beat) | Petals burst UP from the sleeping keeper — one visible petal per counted swing of the run, capped for rendering at a lavish fountain — and stream up and away toward the island in the sky: the count, visibly going home to be BANKED. The round summary card rises with them (next section). This is the mode's signature image and its thesis in one gesture: you fell, and everything you did is flying home without you, safe
4 · The wake | The sleeping form dissolves into the petal stream entirely; the keeper's screen blooms pink-white, the gate chime resolves, and they wake at home — at the Root Plaza, under the Tree, companion stretching beside them — with the summary still on screen. No corpse, no ragdoll, no respawn timer. The fall costs a keeper their RUN and nothing else, ever
5 · The party's fall | When the LAST keeper of a party falls, the valley gets its final shot, held two extra seconds before their wake: the hill crystal, seen from the summit, holding its color against the dark a moment — with the round's Hill Time burning in it — then dimming as the horde takes the empty summit and the fog closes over the roads. Then petals, then home. A full party wipe is a shared ending and is choreographed like one
Record | What it shows | Where it lives

The three Colosseum laws:  1) LIVE COSTS, REPLAY IS FREE — no one is ever locked out of the story; they are only ever paying for the live moment, the best cameras, and a clean screen. 2) CONTESTANTS ARE NEVER PAID ROBUX — a game cannot hand Robux to its players, and this package will not pretend otherwise: ticket money belongs to the game account; the prize pool contestants fight for is Spend Balance, funded at a published rate (below). 3) PREDICTIONS ARE NEVER BETTING — picking a winner is free, always, for every spectator, paid or not. 		if c.Alive then n += 1 end
	end
	return n
end

local function broadcast()
	local roster = {}
	for p, c in pairs(state.Contestants) do
		table.insert(roster, {
			Name = p.Name,
			Alive = c.Alive,
			HillTime = math.floor(c.HillTime),
		})
	end
	remote:FireAllClients("State", {
		Phase = state.Phase,
		MatchId = state.MatchId,
		Pool = state.Pool + state.Rollover,
		Alive = aliveCount(),
		Roster = roster,
	})
end

-- ---------- pay-to-view entitlement (Chapter 46) ----------------
function _G.JadeColosseumHasLiveAccess(player)
	if state.Contestants[player] then return true end -- fighters are in
	if state.Tickets[player] == state.MatchId then return true end
	local day = state.DayPassUntil[player]
	if day and os.time() < day then return true end
	if state.SeasonCache[player] == nil and CONFIG.SeasonPassId > 0 then
		local ok, owns = pcall(function()
			return MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync(
				player.UserId, CONFIG.SeasonPassId)
		end)
		state.SeasonCache[player] = ok and owns or false
	end
	return state.SeasonCache[player] == true
end

-- Called ONLY by Script 10's ProcessReceipt, once per PurchaseId.
function _G.JadeColosseumGrantTicket(player, productId)
	if productId == CONFIG.TicketProductId and CONFIG.TicketProductId > 0 then
		state.Tickets[player] = state.MatchId + (state.Phase == "Live" and 0 or 1)
		return true
	elseif productId == CONFIG.DayPassProductId and CONFIG.DayPassProductId > 0 then
		state.DayPassUntil[player] = os.time() + 24 * 3600
		return true
	end
	return false
end

-- ---------- the prize: pool + ticket-funded bonus -------------
local function payWinner(winner)
	local pool = state.Pool + state.Rollover
	state.Pool, state.Rollover = 0, 0
	if pool > 0 and _G.JadeGrantBonus then
		-- Script 13 clamps one grant to 500; pay in honest chunks.
		local left = pool
		while left > 0 do
			local chunk = math.min(left, 500)
			_G.JadeGrantBonus(winner, chunk, "ColosseumWinner")
			left -= chunk
		end
	end
	remote:FireAllClients("Winner", { Name = winner.Name, Pool = pool })
end

-- ---------- match flow ------------------------------------------
local function eliminate(player, _cause)
	local c = state.Contestants[player]
	if not c or not c.Alive or state.Phase ~= "Live" then return end
	c.Alive = false
	if aliveCount() == 1 then
		for p, cc in pairs(state.Contestants) do
			if cc.Alive then
				state.Phase = "Finished"
				payWinner(p)
			end
		end
	elseif aliveCount() == 0 then
		-- The zombies took everyone: NO winner, and all-or-nothing
		-- means exactly that -- the whole pool rolls to next match.
		state.Phase = "Finished"
		state.Rollover += state.Pool
		state.Pool = 0
		remote:FireAllClients("NoWinner", { Rollover = state.Rollover })
	end
	broadcast()
end
_G.JadeColosseumEliminate = eliminate

local function startMatch()
	local n = 0
	for _ in pairs(state.Contestants) do n += 1 end
	if n < CONFIG.MinContestants then return false end
	state.MatchId += 1
	state.Phase = "Live"
	state.Predictions = {}
	for player, c in pairs(state.Contestants) do
		c.Alive = true
		c.HillTime = 0
		local char = player.Character
		local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
		if hum then
			hum.Died:Connect(function() eliminate(player, "Fell") end)
		end
		local spawn = workspace:FindFirstChild("ColosseumSpawn_" .. ((n % 8) + 1))
		local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if spawn and root then root.CFrame = spawn.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0) end
		n -= 1
	end
	broadcast()
	return true
end
_G.JadeColosseumStart = startMatch

-- ---------- client actions (all re-checked) ---------------------
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action, arg)
	local now = os.clock()
	if lastAction[player] and now - lastAction[player] < 1 then return end
	lastAction[player] = now

	if action == "EnterContest" then
		if state.Phase ~= "Lobby" then return end
		local count = 0
		for _ in pairs(state.Contestants) do count += 1 end
		if count >= CONFIG.MaxContestants or state.Contestants[player] then return end
		local tier = (arg == 2) and CONFIG.BuyIns[2] or CONFIG.BuyIns[1]
		-- Qualifiers enter free: Script 41/42 grant the item.
		local qualified = _G.JadeGetItem and _G.JadeGetItem(player, "ColosseumToken") or 0
		if qualified > 0 then
			_G.JadeGrantItem(player, "ColosseumToken", -1)
			state.Contestants[player] = { Alive = false, BuyIn = 0, HillTime = 0 }
		elseif _G.JadeSpendThrusts and _G.JadeSpendThrusts(player, tier, "ColosseumBuyIn") then
			state.Contestants[player] = { Alive = false, BuyIn = tier, HillTime = 0 }
			state.Pool += tier
		end
		broadcast()

	elseif action == "Predict" then
		-- FREE. Spectators only; locked once Wave 3 begins is
		-- enforced by Script 29/31 calling JadeColosseumLockPicks,
		-- after which this branch refuses (Phase stays Live but
		-- PicksLocked is set server-side).
		if state.Contestants[player] then return end
		if state.PicksLocked then return end
		for p in pairs(state.Contestants) do
			if p.Name == arg then
				state.Predictions[player] = p
				return
			end
		end

	elseif action == "EnterLiveStands" then
		-- The pay-to-view gate itself: no entitlement, no teleport.
		if not _G.JadeColosseumHasLiveAccess(player) then
			remote:FireClient(player, "NeedTicket", {
				TicketProductId = CONFIG.TicketProductId,
				DayPassProductId = CONFIG.DayPassProductId,
				SeasonPassId = CONFIG.SeasonPassId,
			})
			return
		end
		local stands = workspace:FindFirstChild("ColosseumStandsSpawn")
		local root = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if stands and root then root.CFrame = stands.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0) end
		remote:FireClient(player, "LiveAccess", { MatchId = state.MatchId })
	end
end)

function _G.JadeColosseumLockPicks()
	state.PicksLocked = true
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	state.Contestants[player] = nil
	state.Predictions[player] = nil
	state.Tickets[player] = nil
	state.DayPassUntil[player] = nil
	state.SeasonCache[player] = nil
	lastAction[player] = nil
	if state.Phase == "Live" then eliminate(player, "Left") end
end)

-- ---------- VIEW CREDIT — the loyalty loop (Chapter 47) --------
-- Earned ONLY by Sales Vault spend (Script 51 calls the grant
-- below, from Script 10's completed receipts): 1 Robux spent in
-- the Vault = 1 View Credit. Watching live on credit burns
-- 1 credit per minute, times the match's popularity multiplier
-- (Chapter 47's calibration table). Credit is never sold, never
-- transferred, never wagered, and never expires; the balance is
-- capped at 600 so the bank stays a treat, not a second wallet.
local VIEW_CAP = 600
local viewCredit = {} -- [Player] = minutes banked
-- View Credit NEVER expires (Chapter 47), so the bank is persisted
-- like every other promise in this game: a DataStore record per
-- player, loaded on join and saved whenever the balance moves.
-- Without this, "never expires" would quietly mean "until logout".
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local creditStore = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("JadeSpirit_ViewCredit_v1")
local function saveCredit(player)
	local balance = viewCredit[player]
	if balance == nil then return end
	pcall(function()
		creditStore:SetAsync("credit_" .. player.UserId, balance)
	end)
end
local creditWatchers = {} -- [Player] = true while burning credit
state.Popularity = 1.0 -- set at match start: 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 2.0

function _G.JadeGrantViewCredit(player, robuxSpent)
	if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then return end
	robuxSpent = math.floor(tonumber(robuxSpent) or 0)
	if robuxSpent <= 0 then return end
	viewCredit[player] = math.min(VIEW_CAP, (viewCredit[player] or 0) + robuxSpent)
	saveCredit(player)
	remote:FireClient(player, "ViewCredit", { Balance = viewCredit[player] })
end

function _G.JadeGetViewCredit(player)
	return viewCredit[player] or 0
end

function _G.JadeSetPopularity(mult)
	if mult == 1.25 or mult == 1.5 or mult == 2.0 then
		state.Popularity = mult
	else
		state.Popularity = 1.0
	end
end

-- A second listener on the same RemoteEvent: credit entry.
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action)
	if action == "EnterStandsOnCredit" then
		if state.Contestants[player] then return end
		if _G.JadeColosseumHasLiveAccess(player) then return end -- tickets first: they never burn credit
		if (viewCredit[player] or 0) < 10 then
			remote:FireClient(player, "ViewCredit", {
				Balance = viewCredit[player] or 0, Denied = true,
			})
			return
		end
		local stands = workspace:FindFirstChild("ColosseumStandsSpawn")
		local root = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if stands and root then
			root.CFrame = stands.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
			creditWatchers[player] = true
			remote:FireClient(player, "LiveAccess", { MatchId = state.MatchId, OnCredit = true })
		end
	end
end)

-- The burn loop + the match-duration log (Chapter 47 calibration:
-- Script 49 records every match's real duration; the planning
-- model is re-based on the MEDIAN of the last 20, never the mean).
local matchStartedAt = nil
local durationLog = {}
local _startMatch = _G.JadeColosseumStart
_G.JadeColosseumStart = function()
	local ok = _startMatch()
	if ok then matchStartedAt = os.clock() end
	return ok
end

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(60)
		if state.Phase == "Live" then
			for player in pairs(creditWatchers) do
				local cost = 1 * state.Popularity
				viewCredit[player] = math.max(0, (viewCredit[player] or 0) - cost)
				saveCredit(player)
				remote:FireClient(player, "ViewCredit", { Balance = viewCredit[player] })
				if viewCredit[player] < 1 then
					creditWatchers[player] = nil
					remote:FireClient(player, "CreditEmpty", {})
				end
			end
		end
		if state.Phase == "Finished" and matchStartedAt then
			table.insert(durationLog, math.floor(os.clock() - matchStartedAt))
			matchStartedAt = nil
			creditWatchers = {}
			if #durationLog >= 20 then
				local sorted = table.clone(durationLog)
				table.sort(sorted)
				warn(("[Jade Spirit] Colosseum median match (last 20): %ds")
					:format(sorted[math.ceil(#sorted / 2)]))
				durationLog = {}
			end
		end
	end
end)

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	local ok, saved = pcall(function()
		return creditStore:GetAsync("credit_" .. player.UserId)
	end)
	if ok and type(saved) == "number" then
		viewCredit[player] = math.clamp(saved, 0, VIEW_CAP)
	end
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	saveCredit(player)
	viewCredit[player] = nil
	creditWatchers[player] = nil
end)

-- Popularity, set at every match start from the Character Value
-- board (Script 53, Chapter 48) -- counted ranks, not opinions:
-- any contestant ranked 4-10 = Featured 1.25; ranked 1-3 =
-- Star 1.5; two or more ranked 1-3 = Marquee 2.0 (Chapter 47).
local _startWithRate = _G.JadeColosseumStart
_G.JadeColosseumStart = function()
	local mult = 1.0
	if _G.JadeGetValueBoard then
		local ranks = {}
		for _, entry in ipairs(_G.JadeGetValueBoard()) do
			ranks[entry.Name] = entry.Rank
		end
		local top3, top10 = 0, 0
		for player in pairs(state.Contestants) do
			local r = ranks[player.Name]
			if r and r <= 3 then top3 += 1
			elseif r and r <= 10 then top10 += 1 end
		end
		if top3 >= 2 then mult = 2.0
		elseif top3 >= 1 then mult = 1.5
		elseif top10 >= 1 then mult = 1.25 end
	end
	_G.JadeSetPopularity(mult)
	return _startWithRate()
end

-- Phase getter for the tuning system (Chapter 50): adjustments
-- may only land between matches, and this is how they know.
function _G.JadeColosseumPhase()
	return state.Phase
end

-- Jade Spirit | 51_SalesVault.server.lua
-- What it does: THE SALES VAULT (Chapter 47) -- the monetization
-- hub. Owns the weapon-skin catalogue, ownership, and equipping.
--
-- COSMETIC LAW (Chapters 44 and 47): a skin changes materials,
-- colours, and trail presentation ONLY. Damage (25, Script 2),
-- reach, arc, cooldown, and hitboxes are read from the weapon's
-- own table in Scripts 2/43 and are never touched here. This
-- script writes one attribute -- EquippedSkin_<Weapon> -- and
-- presentation systems read it. That is the whole of its power.
--
-- MONEY LAW: skins are Developer Products at 80 Robux (the
-- $0.99 tier, Chapter 47) with PERMANENT ownership recorded from
-- Script 10's receipts -- Script 10 routes each skin's product
-- ID to _G.JadeVaultGrantSkin, once per PurchaseId (Chapter 14).
-- Every granted skin also grants VIEW CREDIT (Chapter 47's
-- loyalty loop): 1 Robux spent = 1 minute of Colosseum view
-- time, through Script 49's JadeGrantViewCredit.
-- Oakley's Golden Dragon Rifle has NO skin, NO product, and NO
-- entry in this catalogue, and never will (Chapters 9 and 36).

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

-- ProductId 0 = not yet created in the Dashboard (Chapter 47's
-- setup steps). A skin with ID 0 cannot be prompted or granted.
local SKINS = {

Rule | Exactly
Earning | View Credit is granted by Script 51 at the moment a skin receipt completes — 80 minutes per skin at the 1 Robux = 1 minute ratio. It is granted from completed, deduplicated receipts only (Chapter 14), and the balance is stored in Script 49's DataStore, so it survives logging out: never expires means never expires
The balance UI | Two places, always the same number (Script 49 is its only owner): the Vault panel's balance strip (Chapter 47, above) and the Colosseum panel's credit line (Script 50), which shows minutes banked, the current match's burn rate, and — at under 5 minutes — a plain warning: 'Credit runs out mid-match: you will be moved to the free replay when it does, or any Vault purchase refills the bank'
Spending it | At the ticket gate, ENTER ON CREDIT (Script 50): Script 49 checks tickets first (a ticket holder never burns credit — paid seats are always spent before earned ones), then requires a 10-minute minimum balance, teleports the spectator to the stands, and burns credit per minute at the match's popularity rate (calibration, below)
When it runs out | At zero, the spectator is moved, mid-match and without drama, to the free delayed-replay position, with the panel explaining exactly what happened and the two ways back (a ticket, or any Vault purchase). Nothing is auto-charged, ever — credit running out can never trigger a Robux prompt by surprise
Expiration | None. View Credit does not expire, decay, or reset with seasons. Loyalty that evaporates is a rental, and this is not one
The cap | 600 minutes (10 hours) per player, enforced by Script 49. At the cap, the Vault's price cards say 'View bank full — spend minutes in the stands to make room' BEFORE purchase, so no one ever buys credit they cannot hold. The cap exists so the bank stays a pleasure to spend, not a second wallet to hoard
What it is not | Not a currency: it cannot be transferred, gifted, traded, wagered (predictions stay free, Chapter 46), converted to Shards, Spend, or Robux, or bought directly at any price. The only door in is a Vault purchase; the only door out is a seat at a live match

VALUE = ½ × SwingScore + ¼ × TimeScore + ¼ × ClosetScore  SwingScore = Lifetime swings ÷ 10. TimeScore = active playtime minutes × 2. Script 53 computes it on the server from records — Script 13's Lifetime, its own activity-verified playtime log, and Script 51's closet count — and republishes the board every minute. -- Jade Spirit | 53_CharacterValue.server.lua
-- What it does: CHARACTER VALUE, the prestige ranking
-- (Chapter 48). One number, three measured factors, computed
-- server-side from records that already exist:
--   VALUE = 0.50 x SwingScore + 0.25 x TimeScore + 0.25 x ClosetScore
--   SwingScore  = Lifetime swings / 10            (Script 13)
--   TimeScore   = ACTIVE playtime minutes x 2     (this script)
--   ClosetScore = rarity points of owned closet   (Script 51
--                 for skins; this table for other cosmetics)
-- A minute of playtime counts only if the character moved more
-- than 5 studs in it -- an AFK keeper is present, not playing,
-- and prestige pays for playing. Clients receive the finished
-- board and nothing else; no client input reaches this math.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("JadeSpiritValue_v1")
local playMinutes, lastPos, moved = {}, {}, {}
local board = {}

local CLOSET_POINTS = { Grove = 100, Blossom = 250, Crystal = 500, Eternal = 1000, Singular = 2500 }
-- Rarity of the permanent cosmetics outside the Vault, by their
-- Chapter 6/28/31/35 catalogue entries. Consumables never count.
local OTHER_CLOSET = {
	OwnsPetalTrailPack = "Grove", OwnsGoldenSpearSkin = "Blossom",
	OwnsBloomAuraEffects = "Blossom", OwnsSakuraQueenSkin = "Crystal",
	OwnsExtraPetSlot = "Crystal", OwnsDaemonDesignPack = "Eternal",
	OwnsTwilightReaperPack = "Eternal", OwnsGroveVIP = "Crystal",
}

local remote = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("JadeValue")
if not remote then
	remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	remote.Name = "JadeValue"
	remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end

local function closetScore(player)
	local total = 0
	for attr, tier in pairs(OTHER_CLOSET) do
		if player:GetAttribute(attr) then total += CLOSET_POINTS[tier] end
	end
	if _G.JadeGetClosetRarity then
		-- Script 51 returns skin points; the loop above already
		-- counted attribute cosmetics, so pass 0 extra.
		total += _G.JadeGetClosetRarity(player, 0)
	end
	-- The ONE Singular closet item in the game is a form, not a
	-- purchase: Oakley's skeleton is displayed as the Legend
	-- (Chapter 48), above and outside this ranked board.
	return total
end

local function compute(player)
	local lifetime = _G.JadeGetLifetime and _G.JadeGetLifetime(player) or 0
	local swingScore = math.floor(lifetime / 10)
	local timeScore = (playMinutes[player] or 0) * 2
	local closet = closetScore(player)
	local value = math.floor(0.50 * swingScore + 0.25 * timeScore + 0.25 * closet)
	return {
		Name = player.Name, Value = value,
		Swings = swingScore, Time = timeScore, Closet = closet,
		Lifetime = lifetime, PlayMinutes = playMinutes[player] or 0,
	}
end

local function publish()
	board = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		table.insert(board, compute(p))
	end
	table.sort(board, function(a, b) return a.Value > b.Value end)
	for rank, entry in ipairs(board) do
		entry.Rank = rank
		local p = Players:FindFirstChild(entry.Name)
		if p then
			p:SetAttribute("CharacterValue", entry.Value)
			p:SetAttribute("ValueRank", rank)
		end
	end
	remote:FireAllClients("Board", board)
end
_G.JadePublishValue = publish
_G.JadeGetValueBoard = function() return board end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	local ok, data = pcall(function() return store:GetAsync("u_" .. player.UserId) end)
	playMinutes[player] = (ok and data and tonumber(data.PlayMinutes)) or 0
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
		local root = char:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 10)
		if root then lastPos[player] = root.Position end
	end)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	pcall(function()
		store:SetAsync("u_" .. player.UserId, { PlayMinutes = playMinutes[player] or 0 })
	end)
	playMinutes[player], lastPos[player], moved[player] = nil, nil, nil
end)

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(60)
		for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
			local root = p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
			if root and lastPos[p] then
				if (root.Position - lastPos[p]).Magnitude > 5 then
					playMinutes[p] = (playMinutes[p] or 0) + 1
				end
				lastPos[p] = root.Position
			end
		end
		publish()
	end
end)

-- Jade Spirit | 55_LiveTuning.server.lua
-- What it does: ADAPTIVE BALANCING (Chapter 50). Other scripts
-- report finished rounds and sales to this script; it keeps the
-- measured record in a DataStore, and — only between matches,
-- only in small steps, only inside the caps below — publishes
-- tuning factors that Scripts 29/31 (waves), 42 (difficulty),
-- and 13 (rewards) read through _G.JadeTuning at the three
-- patch points Chapter 50 lists.
--
-- THE NEVER LIST (Chapter 50): this script has no code path
-- that can touch base damage (25), any price, the gate ladder,
-- pet thresholds, buy-ins, the 1:1 view-credit ratio, the
-- popularity multipliers, or the UserId locks. The caps below
-- are constants, not settings: changing them means editing
-- this file, in daylight, like any other design change.

local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("JadeSpiritTuning_v1")
local CAPS = {
	WardFactor = { Min = 0.85, Max = 1.15, Step = 0.05, Start = 1.0 },
	RewardFactor = { Min = 0.90, Max = 1.10, Step = 0.05, Start = 1.0 },
	LullSeconds = { Min = 45, Max = 75, Step = 5, Start = 60 },
}
local tuning = {}
for key, c in pairs(CAPS) do tuning[key] = c.Start end
local metrics = {
	Rounds = 0, Survival = {}, Frees = 0, Swings = 0,
	DifficultyPicks = {}, ViewEarned = 0, ViewBurned = 0, Sales = {},
}

local remote = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("JadeTuning")
if not remote then
	remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	remote.Name = "JadeTuning"
	remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
end

function _G.JadeTuning(key)
	return tuning[key] or 1
end

-- Called by Scripts 29/31/42 at round end (Chapter 50 patch list).
function _G.JadeReportRound(mode, seconds, frees, difficulty)
	metrics.Rounds += 1
	table.insert(metrics.Survival, math.floor(seconds or 0))
	metrics.Frees += frees or 0
	if difficulty then
		metrics.DifficultyPicks[difficulty] = (metrics.DifficultyPicks[difficulty] or 0) + 1
	end
end

-- Called by Script 51 beside every Vault credit grant.
function _G.JadeReportSale(productKey, robux)
	metrics.Sales[productKey] = (metrics.Sales[productKey] or 0) + (robux or 0)
	metrics.ViewEarned += robux or 0
end

local function median(list)
	if #list == 0 then return 0 end
	local s = table.clone(list)
	table.sort(s)
	return s[math.ceil(#s / 2)]
end

local function stepToward(key, target)
	local c = CAPS[key]
	local cur = tuning[key]
	if target > cur then tuning[key] = math.min(cur + c.Step, c.Max)
	elseif target < cur then tuning[key] = math.max(cur - c.Step, c.Min) end
end

-- The adjustment pass: runs when 20 new rounds are banked,
-- never during a live match (Script 49's phase is the gate).
function _G.JadeTuningPass()
	if metrics.Rounds < 20 then return end
	if _G.JadeColosseumPhase and _G.JadeColosseumPhase() == "Live" then return end
	local med = median(metrics.Survival)
	-- Survival bands vs the 11-minute planning anchor (Chapter 47):
	-- dying too fast means the horde is over-tuned; living far past
	-- the top band means it is under-tuned. Inside the band: hold.
	if med < 240 then stepToward("WardFactor", 0.85); stepToward("LullSeconds", 75)
	elseif med > 900 then stepToward("WardFactor", 1.15); stepToward("LullSeconds", 45) end
	-- Reward pacing: frees per round against the faucet ceilings
	-- of Chapter 6 — tuning may ease rewards by one step, never
	-- past the caps, and never below the promised floors.
	local freesPerRound = metrics.Frees / math.max(metrics.Rounds, 1)
	if freesPerRound > 300 then stepToward("RewardFactor", 0.90)
	elseif freesPerRound < 60 then stepToward("RewardFactor", 1.10) end
	metrics.Rounds, metrics.Survival, metrics.Frees = 0, {}, 0
	remote:FireAllClients("Tuning", tuning)
	pcall(function() store:SetAsync("current", tuning) end)
	warn(("[Jade Spirit] Tuning pass: Ward x%.2f, Rewards x%.2f, Lull %ds (median survival %ds)")
		:format(tuning.WardFactor, tuning.RewardFactor, tuning.LullSeconds, med))
end

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(300)
		_G.JadeTuningPass()
	end
end)

print("[Jade Spirit] Live Tuning ready -- bounded, between matches, never the promises.")
